header.title: Papyrus Leiden I 343 + I 345: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Medical papyri
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:sawmedizin:papyrus-leiden-i-343-i-345:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.1.72: sꜣmꜥnꜣ (samana) is a disease demon with a foreign name. Mauria, Iratiqana and Qiti are foreign names, vocalised by guess; ⸢m⸣ before Mauria is damaged and its function is unclear. dny is obscure (perhaps 'share' or a foreign word). ꜥntj is taken as the goddess Anat, consort of Seth; ꜥmry is unexplained, perhaps a Semitic word (possibly 'Amorite woman').
notes.1.13: kꜣtp is partly damaged and unexplained; evidently a weapon, perhaps a foreign word. sꜣmꜥnꜣ (samana) is a disease demon.
notes.2.52: ꜥḫw is a disease demon or affliction, otherwise unidentified. hrp 'submerge, sink' is taken in a passive sense; the line's syntax is uncertain.

nodes.text: The scimitar of Seth is against you, O *samana*; the *kꜣtp* of Baal is on your head, O *samana*; the copper of Horus is on your brow.
Do you not know me, O *samana*-demon?
See, it is Mauria(?) who knows me, namely:
'I belong to the *dny* of Iratiqana(?), those who speak with the snakes, who slay the snakes, who put an end to the breath of Qiti(?), their mother.'
See, I have sucked at the breasts of Anat, the great *ꜥmry* of Seth.
The *ꜥḫw*, the one who is [eating], while he is sunk down, the dog that gnaws bones!
